title: Best Solutions for Agentic Customer Onboarding
summary: It’s hard for CSMs to run 1:1 onboarding for every account. Agentic onboarding tools let AI show workflows in the real product UI and answer questions.
body_markdown:
When you think about it, a customer success manager’s job sounds eerily similar to an SE’s. They give demos, they answer questions, and they get customers excited about using your product.


And like SEs, the more accounts on their list, the harder it becomes to do hands-on onboarding sessions for every single customer.


So it’s no surprise that many CSMs (like SEs) are turning to agentic tools to help them manage their workflows.


[Agentic demos](https://www.navattic.com/blog/what-are-agentic-demos) can answer customer questions and walk users through real workflows in the product UI so customers can onboard themselves on their own time. Plus, CSMs can review the transcripts later, identify where users got stuck, and do a more personal, in-depth follow-up.


In this post, we’ll explain how agentic onboarding works, what to look for in a tool, and how to get your own agents up and running.


What is agentic customer onboarding?


Agentic customer onboarding is what it sounds like: AI agents guide customers through your product, highlighting specific features and pausing to field customer questions along the way.


Unlike[digital adoption platforms or help center chatbots](https://www.navattic.com/blog/interactive-demos-onboarding-and-training) , agents can actually navigate a clone of your product.


Which means if a user has a question about something the agent hasn’t presented yet, it won’t just send them to a static help article. The agent will jump straight to that area of the product, show a real use case in action, and answer any subsequent questions right then and there.


And because you set the guardrails, the[AI demo](https://www.navattic.com/blog/what-is-an-ai-demo) won’t show anything that’s off-limits (aka not-yet-released features) or currently under construction.


### What should you use agentic customer onboarding for?


Agentic customer onboarding is particularly useful for SMB and long-tail accounts, since those customers often don’t get as much of a white-glove experience.


Agents give them a built-in product expert who can guide them through the platform and answer questions along the way, escalating anything they can’t answer to a CSM.


Agents are just as useful in the opposite direction, too – onboarding multiple teams at an enterprise account.


Each team may have its own workflows and questions, and getting through them all can take up a big chunk of time.


Sending an agentic demo before hopping on a call with several teams can make everyone more prepared and productive.


What to look for in an agentic onboarding tool


There are a ton of chat-based products out there, but most of them feel like Claude or ChatGPT.


And you don’t just want to give your users text-based answers (they could just go look at your docs for that).


Instead, you want a dynamic experience, where an agent can *show* how your product works.


Once you’ve crossed that hurdle, you’ll want to narrow down your list to platforms that:


- **Have built-in knowledge management.** You should be able to provide all kinds of context—files, URLs, and flows—and the tool should be able to sort and learn from them accordingly. Also look for an auto-refresh feature so that the agent is always working from your most up-to-date product information.
- **Allow you to test before launch.** This is a must, as onboarding is most users’ first-ever interaction with your product. You want confidence that the agent will give clear, concise answers and show off your product appropriately.
- **Hand off to a human CSM.** If the agent doesn’t know the answer to a question, it should absolutely not make it up. It should direct the customer to their CSM and, ideally, send that CSM a notification on Slack or Teams (with context from the demo) so they can follow up.
- **Provide transcripts.** Any knowledge gaps that come up in chats with users should funnel back to support teams so they can improve customer content and fine-tune the agent over time.
- **Have multi-language support.** The whole point of agentic customer onboarding is to be self-serve. So if you serve an international audience, your agent demos should be available in any language, 24/7.


Best solutions for agentic customer onboarding


Not sure where to start?


Here’s a shortlist of the best agentic customer onboarding tools on the market, along with their pros and cons:


### Navattic Agents (agentic demos)


[Navattic’s AI agents](https://www.navattic.com/product/agent-demos) run fully autonomous conversations that demo key workflows, answer questions, and show content in real time.


Customers can ask questions aloud or type them into a chat to start learning.


And you can[customize your Navattic Agents’](https://www.navattic.com/blog/best-ai-demo-software) objectives, tone, and personality – plus choose a specific AI avatar or chat widget.


**Best for:** Companies that need a way to prime their users without burning out their CS team


**Key features:**


- **A deep, well-constructed[Knowledge Base](https://docs.navattic.com/agents/build/knowledge) .** You can feed Navattic Agents virtually any kind of file: a URL, plain text, Word docs, Markdown files, slides, or PDFs, and it will convert it into a format the Agent can read and learn from. Sources are organized into folders, where you can edit, refresh, download, remove, or flag them as outdated. You also have full control over whether the Agent can present an asset, share it, or learn from it.
- **Granular[Simulations](https://docs.navattic.com/agents/build/simulations) .** You can run scripted conversations against Navattic Agents to confirm they behave as you expect *before* you launch them to customers. Specify persona, max turns, questions, buyer actions, and other criteria to make sure your Agents respond appropriately.
- **Full transcripts.** CSMs can see exactly where users are getting stuck and step in with helpful information.
- **Context awareness.** Navattic Agents track the thread of a conversation so answers build on what the customer asked already instead of resetting each turn. *“The AI bot’s capability to understand the context and respond accordingly is really good, which makes the overall experience feel more natural and useful.”* ([G2 review](https://www.g2.com/products/navattic/reviews/navattic-review-13870219) )


**Limitations:**


- **Setup.** There is some configuration on the frontend to ensure your Agent has all the information it needs to provide accurate answers in the format and style you want.
- **Runs alongside your product, not inside it.** Agents demo pre-captured flows, so users watch and ask questions instead of clicking through their own live account.


**G2 rating:** 4.8/5 (1,167 ratings)


### Fin (in-app AI assistant)


Fin is an always-on chatbot embedded into your product.


According to their own chatbot on their website, Fin can “welcome new users, clarify their needs, answer common onboarding questions, guide them through your product, and connect them to helpful resources while following your brand voice and policies.”


**Best for:** Teams that want onboarding handled inside of their product, especially those that already use Intercom or Salesforce Service Cloud for support


**Key features:**


- **In-app assistance.** As customers move through each stage of onboarding and learn more about your product, Fin will adjust its approach, highlighting new features while staying within your boundaries. *“I enjoy working hand in hand with AI, as it takes off a lot of load that can be quickly resolved and lets the team focus on the complicated interactions.”* ([G2 review](https://www.g2.com/products/fin/reviews/fin-review-7350999) )
- **Customer insights.** Fin tracks product usage for each account, so CSMs can easily understand adoption and prioritize who they need to focus on.[One G2 user](https://www.g2.com/products/fin/reviews/fin-review-13196970) says, *“Its knowledge base integration, analytics, and continuous learning capabilities reduce support workload, improve response times, and deliver a strong return on investment”*


**Limitations:**


- **Ramp up.** Like most AI tools, the Fin agent needs at least some onboarding itself, such as access to getting started guides, FAQs, call transcripts, and product documentation.
- **Unpredictable usage costs.**[G2 users](https://www.g2.com/products/fin/reviews/fin-review-13052905) say things like, *“What initially started as one price very quickly turned into every month there are extra fees involved,”* and *“Pricing can get expensive if your support volumes are high. Some gray areas around the ‘assumed resolved’ conversations that you are being charged for.”*
- **Hallucinations.** According to some users: *“It can be pretty frustrating when Fin hallucinates, especially when I feel I’ve worded something clearly in the procedure,”* ([G2 review](https://www.g2.com/products/fin/reviews/fin-review-13809312) ) and *“Downside is that it can still get things wrong and hallucinate despite lots of work on our side to inform it.”* ([G2 review](https://www.g2.com/products/fin/reviews/fin-review-14148786) )


**G2 rating:** 4.5/5 (3,982 ratings)


### Qualified (AI assistant)


Typically, Qualified’s agent, Piper, is used as an AI SDR that helps qualify leads and route them to the appropriate rep.


While Piper doesn’t instruct users within your product or show off your product in real time, Piper can help automate parts of the customer onboarding experience.


Per the chatbot on the Qualified website, “Piper can answer common questions in real time on your site, guiding customers to the right resources, and scheduling time with CSMs or specialists when needed.”


**Best for:** Teams that want to automate the conversational, very preliminary side of onboarding (e.g., answering FAQs, routing to CSMs)


**Key features:**


- **Answer onboarding FAQs.** The agent can respond to customers in your logged-in Qualified experience or onboarding pages, answering simple questions and encouraging best practices. *“I really appreciate that Qualified allows us to have someone on the website around the clock, which is helpful because our live chat BDRs don’t work after hours, holidays, or weekends.”* ([G2 review](https://www.g2.com/products/qualified/reviews/qualified-review-12246957) )
- **Route customers to the right owner,** whether that’s support, a named CSM, or implementation folks based on who the customer is and what they say they need. Piper can also schedule 1:1 calls straight from chat, if needed.
- **Send follow-up emails.** After a customer visits a “getting started page” or completes some kind of onboarding activity, Piper can send an email with useful resources to boost adoption rates.


**Limitations:**


- **Doesn’t show off the product.** Users get plain-text answers to their questions instead of seeing how the tool would actually work.
- **Lack of flexibility.**[G2 reviewers](https://www.g2.com/products/qualified/reviews/qualified-review-12219798) say things like, *“While we want to invest in an AI-based strategy, we still want a certain level of control or input into what is generated. Recent updates on the product side have left us with less control on email output…\[so\] we’ve had to figure out workarounds to get the output we want consistently.”*
- **Limited reporting.**[For example](https://www.g2.com/products/qualified/reviews/qualified-review-12223839) : *“Getting highly specific use sometimes requires extra exporting and manual analysis rather than being fully self-served. I would like more visibility into all the error logs, which has been a continuous pain point.”*


**G2 rating:** 4.9/5 (1,580 ratings)


**Note:** Navattic Agents and AI assistants like Fin and Qualified aren’t mutually exclusive. Some Navattic customers have had success[using them together](https://www.navattic.com/blog/how-to-use-qualified-and-navattic-agents-together) .


Also, Fin and Qualified are now owned by Salesforce, so they’re a natural fit if you’re already on Service Cloud or Agentforce.


### Appcues (digital adoption platform)


Appcues is in-app user onboarding software that automatically guides users through parts of your product with multi-step flows, checklists, tooltips, slideouts, banners, pins, and modals.


You can trigger these onboarding steps to happen as users reach certain features, so they’re relevant and timely.


It now also includes Appcues AI, which helps you build out these experiences with an LLM prompt and track user behavior on the backend.


**Best for:** Product-led teams onboarding a high volume of users at once who need structured guidance baked into the product.


**Key features:**


- **AI Workspace,** which you can use to create “Campaigns,” designed to drive a single measurable outcome, such as “get 30% of new trialers create their first project within 10 days.” Explain what you want in plain language, and Appcues will help you build and organize experiences to get you there. *“Appcues stands out because it allows me to cater to various product requests and create different flows and surveys, adapting them seamlessly to different topics and pages as needed.”* ([G2 review](https://www.g2.com/products/appcues/reviews/appcues-review-10361949) )
- **Built-in feedback loops.** Though it doesn’t have an in-app chat function, Appcues can survey your users at key points in their onboarding journey. Those scores feed back to your CSMs, who can intervene before customers churn.
- **Segmentation and analytics.** You can see where users are dropping off, how adoption is going, the paths users take in Appcues and Agentcues flows, and their survey responses. Analytics is accessible through the Appcues MCP.


**Limitations:**


- **Heavy implementation.** Users point out, *“It can get pretty complicated and takes time to build,”* ([G2 review](https://www.g2.com/products/appcues/reviews/appcues-review-11843613) ) and *“I found the implementation process pretty heavy overall. For ease of initial setup, I’d rate it a 3 out of 10.”* ([G2 review](https://www.g2.com/products/appcues/reviews/appcues-review-14034463) )
- **Steep learning curve.** Users say things like, *“The UI is super confusing, and the editor is clunky. Translations are a pain to work with, and triggers take forever to appear,”* and *“The learning curve was steep, I’ve got the hang of it now with AI help.”* ([G2 Review](https://www.g2.com/products/appcues/reviews/appcues-review-14037129) ,[G2 Review](https://www.g2.com/products/appcues/reviews/appcues-review-14030829) )
- **Fiddly editing.** *“The formatting in the editor can be a bit tricky, and some keyboard shortcuts don’t work as expected. Making small edits also takes more time than it should.”* ([G2 review](https://www.g2.com/products/appcues/reviews/appcues-review-14037318) )


**G2 rating:** 4.6/5 (375 ratings)


### UserGuiding (digital adoption platform)


Like Appcues, UserGuiding is also a digital adoption platform.


It has what it calls “Product Tours,” which highlight key product functions with beacons and dialogue boxes. And it also has built-in checklists and surveys.


Unlike Appcues, though, UserGuiding plans come with an AI assistant that can answer users’ questions when they get stuck based on information in your guides, docs, and knowledge base.


**Best for:** Teams that want a mix of in-product tours and a basic built-in assistant


**Key features:**


- **AI assistant targeting.** You can control which pages the assistant appears on, whether it opens by default, and who the assistant gets shown to – specific users or even just yourself for testing purposes.
- **Multilingual support.** UserGuiding’s AI assistant will respond in whatever language users type in. You can also opt to translate widget text, like welcome messages and button labels.
- **Session replay.** On the backend, you can see exactly where users got stuck, what they clicked, and where they went in your product. You can use UserGuiding’s MCP to analyze replays based on user segment or error count to figure out which customers to help first. *“Analytics are helpful for tracking engagement and improving the flows.”* ([G2 review](https://www.g2.com/products/userguiding/reviews/userguiding-review-11726293) )


**Limitations:**


- **Not much feedback on the AI assistant.** As of this writing, there’s only one[G2 review](https://www.g2.com/products/userguiding/reviews/userguiding-review-8082910) about it: *“The strong focus on the AI assistant hasn’t resonated with our needs,”* and the reviewer also mentions *“a noticeable lack of new integrations”* plus a buggy browser extension that *“hinders the creation process.”*
- **Clunky navigation.** Users say things like, *“I think the UX/UI could be improved. Some things are still hard to find in the menu, and I often have to click through multiple sections just to locate what I’m looking for.”* ([G2 review](https://www.g2.com/products/userguiding/reviews/userguiding-review-13061165) )
- **The app is resource-heavy.** *“It consumes a lot of RAM and resources,”* says[one G2 reviewer](https://www.g2.com/products/userguiding/reviews/userguiding-review-9972059) . *“The Chrome extension for editing your Guides has login issues and sometimes needs to be reinstalled to fix them.”*


**G2 rating:** 4.7/5 (782 ratings)


### 1mind (AI sales agent)


[1mind](https://www.navattic.com/blog/best-1mind-alternatives) deploys customizable AI agents they call “Superhumans.”


Originally built as sales agents, 1mind now has two more Superhumans: one to guide users through the product and one that acts as a CSM.


The in-product guide demos and answers user questions on the fly. The Customer Success Superhuman handles check-ins, questions, and booking time with CSMs.


**Best for:** Teams that want a single agent to follow a customer across the whole lifecycle


**Key features:**


- **Understands (and remembers) account history.** Superhumans pass off account information, so the agent that may have talked to a customer when they were a prospect can look back at those conversations, plus notes in your CRM, for full context when speaking with the customer.
- **Proactive engagement.** You can configure your agent to check in with customers, whether they’ve logged a ticket or not.
- **Solid customer success team.** As[one customer puts it](https://www.g2.com/products/1mindai/reviews/1mind-review-11134945) , *“Partnering with 1mind has been an amazing experience. They are highly organized, fast-paced, and deeply committed to understanding and achieving our business goals.”*


**Limitations:**


- **Data gaps.**[One user complains](https://www.g2.com/products/1mindai/reviews/1mind-review-13996446) , *“Conversation tagging doesn’t always match how the chat actually ended. We had chats finish with a meeting booked but still get tagged Support or Other, so they never made it into Salesforce until we caught it. Company capture can also be hit and miss.”*
- **Extensive setup.**[One G2 reviewer](https://www.g2.com/products/1mindai/reviews/1mind-review-13920678) says, *“There is a lot of training needed, and the 1mind team provides hands-on onboarding, does the integration work, and CS continues to support after onboarding with optimization recs and everything.”*[Another shares](https://www.g2.com/products/1mindai/reviews/1mind-review-12072115) , *“Right now, to get the absolute maximum performance, we rely on the 1mind team for certain backend tasks. I’m looking forward to the rollout of the self-service analytics and training portal.”*
- **Minimal ratings.** Though they have a list of case studies on their website, there are only 10 customer reviews on G2 as of this writing.


**G2 rating:** 4.8/5 (10 ratings)


How to launch an onboarding agent


Once you’ve picked your tool, it’s time to train your agent. We recommend starting with several different flavors of onboarding workflows (one to three) based on:


- **Use case.** Different users may have different reasons for buying your product.
- **Industry.** You want any examples to match their typical work.
- **Role.** Again, you want the product to feel customized to their everyday tasks.
- **Product.** If you sell multiple products, it’s a good idea to develop a flow for each one.


From there:


### 1. Load[your agent’s “brain”](https://docs.navattic.com/agents/build/knowledge) with relevant documentation


Videos, slides, help docs, call transcripts – essentially anything you use to train a new customer success manager will all be useful.


Don’t forget to also upload your style guide and product messaging. While these aren’t strictly “sales” demos, adoption is still a form of “selling” users on the product.


### 2. Run your tests


Like with any QA, the goal is not only to test the happy path, but also[to test edge cases](https://docs.navattic.com/changelog/index#agent-simulations-and-photo-avatars) .


In that vein, it’s a good idea to pull in multiple members of the CS team, and even the product team, to make sure you’ve covered your bases.


### 3. Embed it in your onboarding flow


When you feel comfortable with how the agent is working, it’s time to publish.


Consider embedding it directly into your product, so people encounter it the first time they log in.


You could also include[agentic demos](https://www.navattic.com/blog/best-practices-for-sales-agentic-demos) in your welcome emails and help center, so users can access your agent from anywhere.


### 4. Review the results


How are customers using the agent? Are they asking the questions you thought they would?


Are there tweaks you could be making to your agent—or even where you’ve embedded your agent?


Be sure to also measure key adoption metrics, too, to show that your agent is getting people up to speed quicker.
